subject: Cost & latency trade-offs - pricing qualification follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@fintechai.com>, Priya Reddy <priya@fintechai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - cost / latency trade-offs

Hi Samir / Priya -

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the asks we discussed: 

- Usage profile: you mentioned roughly 1-2M tokens/day initially with spikes during batch report generation - peak concurrency roughly 150-250 concurrent inference requests.
- Primary SLO: user-facing assistant responses should be sub-600ms P95 for short prompts (<=256 tokens). Some backend batch jobs can tolerate 2-5s.
- Budget: you flagged a rough monthly budget of $8k- $12k to start and target unit economics around $700-1,000 per 1M tokens depending on latency/throughput.

Immediate next steps (action items):
1) I attached a pricing model (pricing_model.xlsx) showing Hosted vs Dedicated scenarios + expected token math.
2) Vivek - can you review the SLO mapping and suggest batching/streaming config that hits ~600ms P95 for the short prompts and provides cheaper batch throughput for the backfill jobs?
3) Samir/Priya - please confirm average prompt lengths and percent of streaming use (voice assistant vs text) so we can tune streaming vs batch pricing.
4) Procurement: I'll send the MSA and a draft mutual action plan once we lock expected monthly committed tokens.

Attachments: pricing_model.xlsx (detailed unit economics), SOC2_certificate.pdf (security request from call).

Thanks - talk soon,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Samir Shah <samir@fintechai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya@fintechai.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - cost / latency trade-offs

Thanks Marissa - helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Prompt profile: our assistant prompts average ~120 tokens per request; about 60% of requests are short Q&A (<=128 tokens), 30% medium (129-512), 10% long (>512) used in report generation.
- Volume: goal is to ramp to ~1.5M tokens/day within 3 months. Peak concurrency for user-facing flows tends to be 200-250 rps for these short prompts during market open.
- Streaming: only our voice assistant uses streaming (~20% of user-facing traffic). Backend batch jobs (daily reconciliation) are non-streaming and can be queued.
- Budget: $8k- $12k/month is the current working budget - we prefer to hit a target <=$800 per 1M tokens for user-facing traffic, higher tolerance for batch jobs.

Question: do you have a recommended Hosted tier that hits ~600ms P95 at our profile vs when it makes sense to switch to Dedicated reserved capacity?

Best,
Samir
Head of Product, FintechAI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@fintechai.com>, Priya Reddy <priya@fintechai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - cost / latency trade-offs

Great details, thanks Samir - that helps a lot. High-level recommendation based on your profile: 

1) Short term (pilot, 1-3 months): Hosted "Standard" tier with streaming enabled for voice + autoscaling. With our measured latency profiles for models you mentioned and average prompt length (120 tokens), we expect ~500-650ms P95 for short prompts using streaming. Unit economics estimate: ~$800- $950 per 1M tokens for user-facing traffic (includes streaming overhead). See pricing_model.xlsx for scenario A.

2) Medium term (3-12 months, predictable 1.5M+/day): Move to Dedicated reserved capacity (small pool) to reduce unit costs. With Dedicated + optimized batching for backend jobs and kernel selection for your model, we can push unit costs down to ~$550- $700 per 1M tokens while maintaining ~400-550ms P95 for interactive traffic (we trade off some headroom for lower cost).

3) Batching vs streaming guidance:
   - Keep interactive short prompts on streaming with small dynamic batching (batch size target 8-16) to preserve latency.
   - Route non-critical, heavy-throughput jobs to batch queues (larger batch sizes 64-256, no streaming) - these will have much lower unit cost.

4) SLO-driven pricing / options:
   - If you need guaranteed sub-400ms P95, that typically requires higher-tier Dedicated or reserved pre-warmed capacity (premium SLO) and will increase committed cost ~15-25%.
   - We can offer a blended committed rate that gives you a target $/1M token at your chosen P95 band - I included a few blended scenarios in the spreadsheet.

Next steps: 
- Vivek: can you propose batching/streaming config (target batch sizes, KV cache rules) and a rough Dedicated pool spec?
- Samir/Priya: confirm whether the $800 target per 1M is a hard requirement or flexible depending on latency. Once you confirm, I'll draft an MAP and a commitment tier to share with procurement.

Attaching: pricing_model.xlsx, SOC2_certificate.pdf.

Regards,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Samir Shah <samir@fintechai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - cost / latency trade-offs

Thanks for the tag - quick technical notes: 

- For the interactive flows (avg 120 tokens) I recommend streaming with a dynamic batch target of 12 and a soft cap of 24. That will keep P95 in the ~450-600ms window depending on model size and region.
- For batch reconciliation: batch size 128-192, async queue, run in off-peak windows to use spot capacity where possible - expected per-token cost reduction 30-45% vs interactive.
- KV cache: enable LRU prefix caching for common prompts to reduce repeated decode work (saves ~10-15% tokens compute).
- Recommended Dedicated spec (initial): 4 x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent), autoscaling policy to add 2 GPUs with sustained >80% utilization for 10m. This gives good headroom for spikes without overspending.

I'll turn these into a one-pager and a quick cost sensitivity table for the MAP.

- Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
